title: Deterministic page planning eliminates cross-run geometry variance
authors: M. Chen, PhD / A. Okafor, MSc / L. Pereira, PhD
affiliation: Center for Reproducible Documents, Aurora Institute of Technology
abstract: We evaluated whether resolving typed layout constraints before paint improves the reproducibility of scientific documents compiled in WebAssembly.
objective: Compare browser-dependent flow with an explicit page planner using the same manuscript corpus, fonts, physical units, and raster profile.
methods: A preregistered paired benchmark rendered 1,248 structurally diverse documents five times per condition. Page geometry, line breaks, table tracks, and final PNG dimensions were compared.
primaryResult: The planned pipeline produced identical geometry in every eligible run.
interpretation: The effect was strongest in mixed prose-and-table manuscripts, where implicit measurement previously propagated into pagination.
conclusion: Constraint-first planning makes visual output repeatable, inspectable, and suitable for evidence-bearing publishing workflows.
